_meta.source: Port pin is the Quayside Terminal ferry-terminal node from OpenStreetMap (-19.2521, 146.8294). Every POI was resolved individually against OpenStreetMap via Nominatim on 2026-07-30, with the Magnetic Island bays resolved by a bounded query so they return the individual localities rather than the island centroid. Nothing is estimated off a street map. The map spans the city and the island, which between them are the realistic port day; the Great Barrier Reef proper is 40-90 km further offshore and off the map, which is the point the excursions section makes.

port_pin.label: Berth 10, Quayside Terminal — the cruise berth

bbox_hint.note: Townsville sits under Castle Hill on Cleveland Bay, with Magnetic Island 8 km offshore to the north. The cruise berth is in South Townsville; the SeaLink ferry leaves from Breakwater Terminal on the north side of Ross Creek; the Strand runs along the seafront north of the city.

pois.name: Berth 10, Quayside Terminal
pois.notes: Alongside berth on Lennon Drive, South Townsville. Not a tender port since the channel was widened in 2024 — the limit went from 238 m to 300 m. Expect a shuttle out; do not plan on walking.

pois.name: Port of Townsville
pois.notes: A working commercial port. The $251 m Channel Upgrade widened the entrance from 92 m to 180 m; Queen Elizabeth berthed at 294 m in January 2025.

pois.name: Castle Hill
pois.notes: A 286 m pink granite monolith in the middle of the city with a genuine 360-degree panorama — and a sealed road to the top, which makes it one of very few great tropical Queensland views available without a climb. Take a taxi up.

pois.name: The Strand
pois.notes: 2.2 km of seafront with a seawater rockpool that is the safest swim in Townsville year-round, the Ocean Siren sculpture, and the Tobruk Memorial Baths. Stinger enclosure in season.

pois.name: Jezzine Barracks
pois.notes: Heritage parkland at the north end of the Strand, holding the Army Museum of North Queensland and marking both the Wulgurukaba connection to the headland and the site's military history.

pois.name: Flinders Street
pois.notes: The city's main street and its heritage walk — the 1886 Post Office, the 1887-88 Australian Joint Stock Bank, Tattersalls Hotel of 1864, the Great Northern Hotel of 1901. Queensland Museum Tropics is on it, free, daily 9am-4pm.

pois.name: Nelly Bay, Magnetic Island
pois.notes: Where the ferry lands on Magnetic Island, 20-25 minutes from Townsville. The island bus connects it to the other bays.

pois.name: Horseshoe Bay, Magnetic Island
pois.notes: The island's largest bay, with cafés and a stinger enclosure in season. The obvious place to finish the Forts Walk.

pois.name: Arcadia, Magnetic Island
pois.notes: A settlement on the island's east side with a sheltered swimming bay and a pub, and the start of the Forts Walk approach.

pois.name: Picnic Bay, Magnetic Island
pois.notes: The island's original ferry terminal and quietest settlement, at the southern end facing Townsville.

pois.name: Mount Cook, Magnetic Island
pois.notes: The island's highest point at 497 m, within Magnetic Island National Park, which covers about 76% of the island.

pois.name: Billabong Sanctuary
pois.notes: A wildlife sanctuary 17 km south of the city, open daily, about $54 adult. The guaranteed-koala option if you would rather not gamble on the Forts Walk.
